title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 62
paragraphs: While he was still calling on her, the Tegeans sprang forward before the rest and advanced against the barbarians; and immediately after Pausanias's prayer the sacrifices proved favorable for the Lacedaemonians as they offered them. So when at last this came to pass, they too advanced against the Persians; and the Persians put aside their bows and came against them. Then first there was fighting over the wicker shields, and when these had been overturned, the fighting by the temple of Demeter was fierce and went on for a long time, until at last they came to grappling; for the barbarians would seize hold of the spears and break them off. In courage and strength the Persians were not inferior to the others, but they had no defensive armor, and moreover they were unversed in war and unequal to their opponents in skill; they would dart out one at a time or in groups of about ten, some more, some fewer, and fall upon the Spartans and perish.
